channel.title: The Wang Report · HK Local Desk
channel.description: The Wang Report HK Local Desk desk: daily briefings and weekly columns.

item.title: Woodland Garden Salt Water Main Bursts, Floods Lobby
item.description: A ruptured underground main on MacDonnell Road sent a saltwater column into a Mid-Levels lobby at 1am, the kind of infrastructure failure that never makes the five-year plan speeches.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Government Drops Fanling Golf Course Appeal
item.description: Housing officials will not fight a court ruling that killed the Fanling housing plan, so the golf course everyone argued about for a decade just... stays a golf course.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Tse Wants Tougher Rules On Dog Owners After Attack
item.description: A lawmaker is pushing the government to tighten dog ownership rules, and the gap he's pointing at is the same one that let a dangerous dog slip through as a mongrel.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: HK$20 Billion "Green" Bond Comes With No Homes Attached
item.description: The government wants the world's biggest digital green bond while ordinary Hong Kongers still wait for anything green in their own neighbourhood to actually help their bills.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: No Tampering Found In Sports Drinks, Fear Stays Anyway
item.description: Health officials tested the sports drinks everyone got spooked about this week and found nothing wrong, but good luck telling that to a parent standing in the supermarket aisle.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Housing Chief Promises Shorter Queue By 2027
item.description: The public housing wait has been climbing for years and now the government has put a year on the promise to turn it around.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Coach Slaps Kid, Gets A Warning Letter
item.description: An eight-year-old was slapped and made to stand in the sun by his own coach, and the punishment for that is a signed promise to behave.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: 18,000 Taxi Plates, Zero New Cars, One Crackdown Coming
item.description: Hong Kong's promised enforcement push on illegal ride-hailing drivers arrives on top of a taxi fleet that hasn't grown since the medallions were capped.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Fourth Security Chief In A Year Takes The National Security Desk
item.description: Kelvin Kong Hok-lai steps in as the force's national security chief just as police tell the public "soft resistance" is still out there somewhere.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: One Dog Attack, Two Speeds Of Government Response
item.description: A woman died in a suspected dog mauling on Sunday, and by Monday the AFCD had a soundbite ready while the actual loophole in pet ownership law is still just "under review.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Three Robots Argue, HKO Won't Pick A Winner
item.description: Hong Kong's own weather site is showing three AI models split on whether a cyclone brushes the city Saturday, and the Observatory is letting the public referee it themselves.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Five Clean Years Beat A HK$21,000 Guide Badge
item.description: Hong Kong demands five clean licence years before a human can babysit a driverless car in Tseung Kwan O, while a tour guide got three strikes this year before losing her badge for threatening tourists into a jade shop.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Hong Kong Calls The Taxi Crash Permanent
item.description: Hong Kong opened ride-hailing licence applications this week, confirming a taxi licence collapse from HK$7.66 million to HK$2.6 million that the Chief Executive already called irreversible.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: No Cap On Companies, Hard Cap On Seats
item.description: Hong Kong says there's no cap on ride-hailing licences, but a 10,000-vehicle ceiling means the real fight is over who inherits a black market that already exists.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: China Resources Banks $1.53 Billion On 46,921 Rejections
item.description: The Sterling I's record-breaking sellout says more about a well-timed discount than about a housing market finding its footing again.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: AFCD's Dog Chip System Doesn't Check What It Registers
item.description: Hong Kong's dog microchip system records whatever breed an owner claims without checking it, and that gap let a suspected fighting-breed dog register as a mongrel before it killed someone.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Housing Bureau Calls A Worse Wait Good News
item.description: The public housing wait crept to 4.8 years, and the Housing Bureau called it a 'positive sign,' the same week the plan meant to fix it closed for submissions.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Hong Kong Won't Wait Five Minutes For A Train
item.description: Hong Kong won't wait five minutes for a train, but this year's scam numbers show one thing this city will sit through patiently: getting robbed.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Hong Kong's Heat Warning Beat the Housing Transfer Queue
item.description: Hong Kong's government can flag a dangerous temperature within minutes but let a documented, nine-month neighbour dispute run to a fatal stabbing before it moved anyone.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Nine Months Between a Mediation and a Cleaver in Wong Tai Sin
item.description: Hong Kong polices noise complaints with a shrug, and this week in Wong Tai Sin that shrug ended with a cleaver and a body on the podium.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Kai Tak's Roof Opened Cold. Huanggang Needs 10,000 People First
item.description: Kai Tak proved Hong Kong can open a major venue cold; Huanggang's 10,000-person drill requirement says the border's caution is about blame, not safety.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Hong Kong Won't Count Its Own Death Wishes
item.description: The government tracks its own systems to the decimal but won't say how many people signed the new right to refuse resuscitation, which tells you what it thinks of the number.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: The Monkey That Out-Disrupted a Typhoon
item.description: Typhoon Noul took 29 hours, a grounded airline and a live Signal No.10 watch to rattle Hong Kong; a monkey shut the Tsuen Wan Line twice for free.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Cathay Refunds in Hours, Helpers Lose Their Sunday
item.description: Hong Kong's storm machinery refunds Cathay passengers within hours, but offers domestic helpers no make-up day when a typhoon eats their one day off.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: The Water Department's Tai Po Moment
item.description: The same week officials vowed to end self-policed contractor checks after Tai Po, an 18-inch government pipe proved you don't need a contractor to defer maintenance.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Everyone Pays For Tai Po Except Officials
item.description: The inquiry says government shares the blame for the Tai Po fire, but only the contractor gets punished and only the survivors get to leave; that is not accountability.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: A Warning With No Off Switch
item.description: Hong Kong only changes behaviour when a number forces it to, and this week's Very Hot Weather Warning proved it by sending six hikers to hospital.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Hong Kong Will Rescue You, If You Weren't Working
item.description: Hong Kong airlifts hikers to hospital for free when the heat gets them, but the new gig-worker injury law won't cover a rider felled by the same heat.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Bavi Missed HK, 135 Flights Cancelled Anyway
item.description: Typhoon Bavi never touched Hong Kong, yet the city ate a weekend of cancelled flights and record heat, while the same World Cup fever fills a licensed Lan Kwai Fong screen and an illegal Tai Po betting den with identical money.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: HEAL Fertility's Six Weeks of Silence
item.description: A Central fertility clinic mixed up embryo test samples for two couples, and the real scandal is a watchdog with no teeth, not one lab's bad week.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Clear Water Bay's Propeller Strike Under Signal 1
item.description: A confirmed injury at Clear Water Bay under Signal 1 conditions means the Observatory's undecided call on Signal 3 is already beside the point for anyone planning a weekend on the water.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Fifteen Certified Flats, 110,000 Still Illegal
item.description: Hong Kong certified its first legal subdivided flats this week, but at the current pace the whole scheme will price out the very tenants it was built to save.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Wang Chi House's 87.5 Percent
item.description: The undamaged tower at Wang Fuk Court left the buyback deal faster than the burnt ones, which tells you this was never really about fire damage.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Wang Fuk's Sign-Up Order Decides Who Gets Kai Tak
item.description: The 85.6 percent signing rate on the Wang Fuk Court buyback looks like a success story, but the first-come priority system has quietly turned fire survivors into competitors for the same flats.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Wang Fuk's HK$6.8 Billion Lands as Tai Po Flips
item.description: The government just paid 1,600 Wang Fuk families up to HK$10,500 a square foot, right as flippers creep back citywide, and that timing alone should make you squint at the recovery story.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: No Protocol Stopped the 32-Degree Sports Day
item.description: Hong Kong's outdoor event calendar ran at full volume this weekend with no protocol to pause it, and a child died at a sports ground while thousands watched dragon boats on the harbour.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: HK Electric's 33.9% Hike Arrives in August
item.description: HK Electric's 33.9% fuel charge hike lands on summer heat demand precisely because the billing mechanism was always designed to delay bad news, not absorb it.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Free Harbour, Germany at 4 a.m.
item.description: This weekend in Hong Kong, the free TST harbour carnival runs through the day and World Cup football on Now TV runs through the night.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: 21 Indicators, No Record at Lai King
item.description: A 224-page poverty framework released June 18 did not reach the Lai King couple found unconscious with no welfare contact record two days later.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Two Infants in ICU While Venues Open Saturday
item.description: Two unvaccinated infants are in Prince of Wales Hospital's paediatric ICU as authorities warn COVID transmission rises over the next two months; the family weekend opens regardless.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Hop On Has Missed Both Deadlines
item.description: Hop On Management has missed two court-upheld deadlines to convene Wang Fuk Court homeowners while 1,984 displaced households face a June 30 buyback cutoff they cannot collectively scrutinize.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: HK$17 Gate, Queue Before Eight
item.description: The Observatory's extreme heat warning means the public pool queue and the nearest air-conditioned mall are where this Saturday's outdoor plans actually end up.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: 71.5 Per Cent, One Market Short
item.description: May's home-sales-value surge is a wealth-tier event; the secondary market where most HK families buy has not moved with it, and Beijing's capital controls are the reason.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: HK$4.6 Billion Keeps the Counter Open
item.description: Home prices logged an eleventh consecutive monthly gain; the public post office serving the same streets needs HK$4.6 billion from the government to avoid service cuts through next year.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: CLP's June Bill Lands on 18,000 Permit Holders
item.description: The government's proposed 10,000 ride-hailing permits and CLP's 5.4% June fuel increase land on the same operators, who are still paying for the market they expected to keep.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Goldman's 15 Percent, Friday's Gazette
item.description: Goldman's fifteen percent revision hits estate agent windows on the same Friday the civil service investigation regulation lands, handing two very different papers to two very different readers.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Four Certified. 110,000 Still Waiting.
item.description: Four units certified from a backlog of 110,000 illegal flats, as secondary prices are forecast to rise 11% this year: the owners holding unregistered paper are watching a recovery they cannot access.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: The Rate the Recovery Skipped
item.description: Hong Kong's 5.9% Q1 growth is real, IMF-endorsed, and politically settled; it has not reached the credit windows and minimum-order thresholds where small operators run their calculations.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: The Gap the Stall Pays
item.description: Hong Kong printed 5.9 percent GDP growth for Q1 and raised its inflation forecast in the same week; both numbers are accurate, and they reach different addresses.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: The Q1 Number That Lands Unevenly
item.description: Hong Kong's 5.9% Q1 growth and the government's inflation forecast revision arrived in the same week; they do not describe the same households.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: When the Cut Arrives One Generation Late
item.description: The operators who gain from the May toll cut are the same families financing university for children entering a job market down sixty percent.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: What S&P's Eight Percent Does Not Say
item.description: S&P forecasts 8-10% home price growth while New World moves to sell $2 billion in assets, leaving mass-market buyers with two stories that do not add up.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung
